solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flattened like some plants in rose beds prepared with entry for competition

indicators.note: beds that are prepared have been dug over and remade, so the letters are rearranged
an entry is a going-in, so the following item is put inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
comp is a short form of competition

explanation.surface: A gardener's rose beds, readied for a flower show, contain plants flattened under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: OBRESSED, the jumbled rose beds, takes COMP after its first two letters to make OBCOMPRESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Obcompressed is a botanical term for parts flattened front to back, the reverse of the usual direction.

clue.text: Home for many an Indian black deer, acreage fenced in

indicators.note: something fenced in is enclosed, so one letter sits inside the word for a deer

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a hart is a male red deer
A is the abbreviation for acre or acreage

explanation.surface: An Indian blackbuck finds a fenced acre to live in.
explanation.walkthrough: B is followed by HART with A put between its R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Bharat is the Hindi name for India, the official alternative name in its constitution, so it is the homeland of most Indians.

clue.text: Yellowish colour displayed by bread in tin

indicators.note: in places the word for bread within the word for a tin

blocks.note: roti is an Indian flatbread
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A loaf baked in a tin turns a yellowish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotin, or carotene, is the orange-yellow pigment in carrots, and Chambers also gives it as that colouring.

clue.text: I'm pro out sporting? I'd nae shoot this wee bird

indicators.note: sporting suggests playing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
surface padding in Scots, saying the speaker would not shoot such a young bird

explanation.surface: A Scottish professional out shooting refuses to fire at a young bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots voice of the definition (nae, wee) hints that the answer is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A muirpoot is Scots for a young moorfowl, a grouse chick too small for any sporting gun to shoot.

clue.text: The old man accompanying golf club captain

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
Royal Troon is a famous golf club on the Ayrshire coast in Scotland

explanation.surface: Father goes along with the captain of the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain looks like part of the club's officers, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Patroon is an old word for the master or captain of a ship, from the Spanish patrón, a boss.

clue.text: Has coiffure arranged? A frill like this is off, possibly

indicators.note: arranged hair has been set into a new order, as the letters are
possibly hints that the answer and the following words could make up the rearranged letters between them
the words after it are taken away, being off or removed from the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Someone has their hair done, but a frill like this is said to be out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: HAS COIFFURE holds the answer plus A, I, S, O, F, F, so with 'A' and 'is off' taken away, the rest is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a pleated or gathered strip of fabric used as trimming, a kind of frill.

clue.text: Stagger like Scottish drunk, one such swallowing last of flacket

indicators.note: a drinker swallowing something takes it inside, so a letter goes within
'last of' keeps only the last letter of 'flacket'

blocks.note: a drunk is a sot
the final letter of flacket

explanation.surface: A tipsy Scot reels about after draining a flask.
explanation.walkthrough: A flacket is a Scots word for a flask, which suits the drinker. The definition includes 'like Scottish drunk', since stot is a Scots word for a drunk's stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to stot is to bounce or to walk unsteadily, the gait of someone who has had too much.

clue.text: Skier with being regularly deprived? One might get this for a quid

definitions.text: One might get this for a quid

indicators.note: regularly deprived means every second letter is taken away, leaving the others

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A skier sadly loses something; one might buy it for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid looks like a pound sterling, but here it is a wad of something to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirih is betel, the leaf and nut mixture chewed as a quid in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Accipitrines as a group dash above us

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means the first piece is written over, and so before, the second

blocks.note: élan is dash or flair
taken as written

explanation.surface: A collective name for hawks that swoop over our heads.
explanation.walkthrough: Accipitrines are hawks and their kin; dash here is a noun for verve, not a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Elanus is the genus of the white-tailed and black-winged kites, birds of prey of the hawk family Accipitridae.

clue.text: Gentry put out about a vintage, little special (10, two words)

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed, so its letters are shaken up
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the rest

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
per means a, as in so much a head
a cru is a vineyard or its wine, a vintage
S is a short form of special

explanation.surface: Upper-class people are annoyed about the quality of a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' meaning per, as in so much per head, is the hard step; out jumbles only the word put.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper crust is the aristocracy, the top layer of society, just as gentry are the landed upper class.

clue.text: Maori group united after their settlement's returned

indicators.note: returned means going back, so the word for the settlement is read backwards

blocks.note: a pa or pah is a fortified Maori village
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A Maori tribe stays united once its land is given back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hapu is a sub-tribe or clan, a subdivision of a Maori iwi.

clue.text: Give jaunty angle to front of lid and titup friskily around

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
friskily means playfully, so the letters skip into a new order
around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the other one

blocks.note: the opening letter of lid
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tip your hat at a rakish angle and prance about.
explanation.walkthrough: Titup is a real word, meaning to prance or move jauntily, which makes it a natural fit for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To uptilt something is to tilt it upwards, as a cap set at a jaunty angle is.

clue.text: Like some acid? Fussy about right answer if lacking one (10, two words)

indicators.note: lacking one means the numeral-like letter I is dropped from the little word before
about means surrounding, so the word for fussy goes round the rest

blocks.note: tatty can mean fussy in the sense of over-ornate or tawdry
R is the abbreviation for right
ans is the abbreviation for answer
taken as written, then losing a letter

explanation.surface: A picky eater objects to the right answer on a food label.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatty here is the Chambers sense of fussy or over-elaborate, not shabby; the inserted letters go in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trans fatty acids are a kind of unsaturated fat, so an acid can be described with this phrase.

clue.text: Young fish to tickle? It's stirred by thible

blocks.note: a parr is a young salmon
an itch is a tickle on the skin

explanation.surface: A young salmon is tickled out of the water, an old poaching trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickling trout is a poacher's way of catching fish by hand. A thible is a Scots porridge stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Parritch is Scots for porridge, the food a thible or spurtle is used to stir.

clue.text: Amateur trailing one who isn't in vessel

indicators.note: trailing means following behind, so the amateur letter comes second

blocks.note: a professional is someone who is not an amateur
A is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: An amateur sailor follows a professional in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Trailing puts the amateur behind; 'one who isn't' refers back to amateur, so it means a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay sailing boat with an outrigger, a kind of sailing vessel.

clue.text: Heart of sting ray pierced by harpoon's head, at sea? Marine creature now defunct

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters
the head of a word is its first letter
pierced by means something is driven inside, as a harpoon goes into a fish
at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the middle three letters of sting
taken as written
the first letter of harpoon

explanation.surface: A stingray is speared by a harpoon out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The harpoon's head goes inside the ray before everything is mixed; Steller's sea cow was wiped out by 1768.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhytina is the genus of Steller's sea cow, a huge marine mammal hunted to extinction in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Added rolls after central part of meal – don't leave any (5, two words)

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns end to end, so the word is read backwards
the central part of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: the middle two letters of meal
put, as in put in more, means added

explanation.surface: Bread rolls served with the main course, and a parent telling a child to clear the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Eat up is a command to finish everything on the plate, leaving nothing behind.

clue.text: Jaunty esprit in accordance with folk song

indicators.note: jaunty means lively and carefree, so the letters bounce into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to can mean according to, as in to scale

explanation.surface: A lively spirit suits a traditional folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rispetto is an Italian folk song or poem of love in eight-line stanzas.

clue.text: Hot where baskers are lying? Those at ease respond to it

definitions.text: Those at ease respond to it

indicators.note: where baskers are lying places the letter inside the place they lie

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
people who bask lie in the sun

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers lounge in the heat, and soldiers relax.
explanation.walkthrough: At ease is a military stance; soldiers standing at ease snap to attention on the order.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Shun is the drill command, short for attention, given to soldiers standing at ease.

clue.text: Think to break china trinkets? That's fatuity

indicators.note: one word breaks into another, landing in the middle of it

blocks.note: Goss is collectable crested china from Victorian and Edwardian souvenirs
to opine is to think or hold a view

explanation.surface: Imagine smashing ornamental china; how silly that would be.
explanation.walkthrough: Goss china was made by W. H. Goss, souvenir pieces bearing town crests.
explanation.definitionFit: Goopiness is the quality of being goopy, silly or fatuous, so it means fatuity.

clue.text: It may be blended for painter (7, two words)

definitions.text: It may be blended for painter

indicators.note: blended things are mixed together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something an artist mixes into the paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: pine tar is mixed into paints and wood finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine tar, made from pine resin, is blended with oils in paints and wood preservatives.

clue.text: Rhetorical trope this writer's used to follow end of phrase: repetition

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
used to follow puts the setter's self-reference after the other two pieces

blocks.note: the final letter of phrase
learning by rote is learning by repetition
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A writer reaches for a stylistic device to finish a phrase by repeating it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the parts out of their final order, with 'this writer' placed last despite coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroteme, also erotema, is a rhetorical question, a question asked for effect not for an answer.

clue.text: Preserve stone I ground to separate into sections

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bottle fruit stones after crushing them to split them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To cantonise is to divide a country into cantons, administrative districts like those of Switzerland.

clue.text: One with superior manner? She should improve her language! (6, two words)

blocks.note: a means one
up means higher, superior
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A haughty person ought to stop swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improve her language' sounds like cleaning up bad words, but means learning English while living abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner living with a family to help with childcare, typically while learning their language.

clue.text: Part of potboiler, a series with which some writers end?

indicators.note: part of means the letters are a section of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across potboiler, a and series

explanation.surface: A pulp novelist finishes off a cheap book series.
explanation.walkthrough: The writers are pencils, many of which end in a rubber tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Many pencils have a rubber on the end, so an eraser is how some writing tools finish.

clue.text: Parliament disturbance putting us off

indicators.note: putting off means removing, so those two letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a rumpus is a commotion

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene in the House puts voters off politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament was what remained of the Long Parliament after Pride's Purge of 1648.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rump was the shortened English Parliament of 1648 to 1653, so the word names that parliament.

clue.text: Coarse metal, lustreless

blocks.note: first meaning: an impure product of smelting sulphide ores
second meaning: with a dull, non-shiny finish

explanation.surface: Rough metal with no shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Matte is both the crude sulphide mix from smelting copper or nickel, and a dull surface finish.

clue.text: Life, or how it ends, in a mound

indicators.note: where a word ends is its final letter
in places one letter inside the word for a mound

blocks.note: it refers back to the word life, and its final letter is taken
bing is a dialect word for a heap or mound

explanation.surface: Life, and how it finishes, in a burial mound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the word life, so the letter taken is where life ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Being means existence, the state of being alive.

clue.text: Skin condition contained by soaps or antibiotics

indicators.note: contained by means the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across soaps, or and antibiotics

explanation.surface: A rash being treated with soaps or drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Psora is an old term for itchy skin diseases such as scabies or psoriasis.

clue.text: Repute badly affected, adult admitted being in difficulties (7, three words)

indicators.note: badly affected means damaged and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
admitted means let in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: A grown-up whose reputation has been damaged is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Up a tree is an idiom for being stuck in a fix, like a treed animal with no way down.

clue.text: Run in stage of tournament? Have a go, as of old

definitions.text: Have a go, as of old

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word for a stage

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a tie is a match in a knockout round, such as a cup tie

explanation.surface: A score made during one round of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British term for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Trie is an old spelling of try, to attempt or have a go.

clue.text: Rank and file's last worthless stuff

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word before

blocks.note: the final letter of file
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: The ordinary soldiers end up with nothing but junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank and file' reads as one phrase, but rank is the definition and file only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Etat, from French, means a state or rank, as in a social standing.

clue.text: Like the runt after time sow rolled over in roster

indicators.note: rolled over means turned end to end, so the word is read backwards
in places the pieces inside the word for a roster

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an elt is a young sow
a roster is a list

explanation.surface: The smallest piglet comes after the sow has rolled over in its pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest of a litter, so it is the littlest.

clue.text: Reddish-brown monkey with a tail of maroon

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a titi is a small South American monkey
taken as written
the final letter of maroon

explanation.surface: A monkey with a dark red tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is the auburn shade seen in the hair of women painted by Titian.

clue.text: Bell beginning to emit no small volume

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Great Tom is a famous bell, as at Christ Church, Oxford
the opening letter of emit

explanation.surface: A great bell starts to ring out with no small volume of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Volume suggests loudness, but it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy book, so it is a volume of no small size.

clue.text: Such as Verdi Gerry & Co adapted, typical Covent Garden stuff?

indicators.note: adapted means altered to fit, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: verdi is Italian for green, as if the composer's name were a colour
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An opera house staging Verdi with a company led by Gerry.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is both London's opera house and the site of its old fruit and vegetable market, so Verdi suits the surface and greengrocery the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden was London's main fruit and vegetable market until 1974, so fresh produce was its typical stock.
